tldr: The Insights report is where most Mixpanel analysis starts. Pick what to measure, filter the events, break it down by a property, set the timeframe, and choose the chart type. Those five choices cover most of the questions you'll ask day to day.

faq: What is the Insights report used for?
It's the general-purpose report in Mixpanel — counting events, segmenting them by property, and plotting them over time. Most day-to-day questions start here.
What does a breakdown actually do?
Splits your metric by a property, so one line becomes one line per value. It's the difference between knowing how many people signed up and knowing which source they came from.
Which chart type should you use?
Line for anything over time, bar for comparing values at a point, and a number when the trend doesn't matter. Choosing badly is the most common way a correct report gets misread.
